_: Golden for the us.aps-saver-choice-max preset — D2 §9 1 and 4, D9 §3. Arizona's demand charge is the clearest case of eligibility: a bigger hour outside the window is worth nothing.

sources.grammar: HLD §8's US row: APS `(60, on_peak, all, max, month, Linear)` — a 60-minute demand interval, only on-peak hours eligible, the single highest of the month, priced linearly.
sources.hours: aps.com/demand, read 2026-09-19: "the Time-of-Use 4pm-7pm Weekdays with Demand rate plan has a monthly demand charge, which is a charge for your highest hour of energy used between 4pm-7pm weekdays, each billing month". Saver Choice Max is that plan's earlier name; Saver Choice Plus is the frozen 3pm-8pm one.
sources.price: ASSUMED. $19.585/kW summer for the R-3 plan, per APS's tariff as reported secondarily (Decision 79293, effective 2024-03-08); the APS rate-schedule PDF was not read inside this WP's lookup budget. Replaced by the $/kW on the household's own plan sheet.
sources.season: ASSUMED, and it is a grammar limit rather than a reading of the tariff: APS charges a demand rate in winter too, at a lower $/kW, and `PeakTariff` carries one `pricing` and one `eligible` per version, so a summer and a winter rate cannot both be expressed. The preset therefore covers the summer season (May-October), where the charge bites, and a winter month falls through to no capacity component at all — the documented NoPeak degradation (HLD §3) rather than a wrong number. See the preset's `assumed`.
sources.month: Constructed, not measured: July 2026, three on-peak weekday hours and two windows that must be invisible.
sources.metric_kw: per_day = all with per_period = max is the single highest eligible hour: max(5.20, 6.40, 4.10) = 6.40 kW. Arizona does not observe DST, so July local time needs no care.
sources.not_metric_kw: 8.60 kW, the 21:00 window on 2026-07-08. If eligibility were ignored it would be the metric; it is off-peak, so it never enters and never creates a day entry (D2 §5.1, D-0058). The 7.90 kW hour on Saturday 2026-07-11 is invisible for the same reason.
sources.fee: 6.40 kW x 19.585 USD/kW = 125.344 USD for the month.

eligibility.why: one minute before the window opens
January is outside the summer season this version covers

eligible_windows.why: 16:00-19:00 in whole hours is three windows, and that is what D5 may plan into
